title: Ernest P. Worrell: The Accidental Movie Star
description: A Nashville ad man's yokel, a summer camp, a troll army, and a toy box—five steps deep into Ernest.
imageHint: The rubber-faced character in his signature denim vest and baseball cap, ready to cause chaos

questions.question: Ernest P. Worrell leans into the camera and asks his never-quite-seen neighbor what catchphrase?
acceptedAnswers: you know what i mean vern
questions.explanation: The camera is Vern, so we see Ernest the way Vern does: way too close. Vern's disgusted reactions, and his door shutting in Ernest's face, are half the joke.

questions.question: Before "Know what I mean, Vern?" sold movie tickets, it sold everything else. Ernest was born in 1980 in what kind of ad?
questions.explanation: Nashville's Carden & Cherry created him. The first spot plugged the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders at Beech Bend Park, Kentucky; dairies nationwide later ran near-identical Ernest milk ads.

questions.question: Hundreds of commercials made him a movie star. In his first big-screen hit (1987), he's the handyman at a summer retreat for kids. What's the title?
questions.explanation: It made $23.5 million on a $3.5 million budget and stayed in the top five for three weeks. Varney still got a Razzie nomination for Worst New Star.

questions.question: After Camp, Ernest Scared Stupid (1991) unleashes a troll army on the town of Briarville. What everyday drink melts the trolls?
questions.explanation: The kids load Super Soakers with it. Fitting for a guy who spent years selling milk for dairies. The head troll, Trantor, only falls to Ernest's love, and a kiss on his snotty nose.

questions.question: After his milk-powered troll war, Jim Varney landed his best-known voice role, in 1995's Toy Story. Who did he play?
questions.explanation: He voiced Slinky in Toy Story and Toy Story 2. Varney died in 2000, and his friend Blake Clark took over the role from Toy Story 3 on.

easterEgg.title: The P stands for...
easterEgg.text: According to the official Ernest history, the character was invented in 1980 at a creative meeting at Carden & Cherry, and his full name is Ernest P. Worrell, with the P standing for "Power Tools."
